BETWEEN:-
 PRAKASH AHIRWAR S/O SHRI MADAN AHIRWAR,
 AGED ABOUT 27 YEARS, OCCUPATION:

AGRICULTURE  PAMAKHEDI POLICE STATION SANOUDHA, DISTRICT  SAGAR (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI NEERAJ JAIN - ADVOCATE)

AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION BANDA, DISTRICT SAGAR (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 .
 (BY SHRI L.A.S. BAGHEL - DEPUTY GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER

This second application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.518/2022 registered at Police Station Banda, District Sagar, for the offence punishable under Sections 304B, 498A, 34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Earlier application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to move afresh after recording the statements of parents of the deceased vide order dated 30.09.2022.
Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail since 01.06.2022.

It is further submitted that the present applicant was though not involved in any of the alleged crime but merely because presumption goes against him as his wife committed suicide by hanging herself within seven years of marriage and as such after her death, the parents have made allegation that deceased Prakash Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18485313/
1 was being harassed by the present applicant and his family members demanding dowry.

sentences.text:
However,
he submits that it is clear from the prosecution case that the deceased had committed suicide in her maternal home and prior to committing suicide she was in her maternal home for a long period of time of four months.
However, he submits that the deceased had committed suicide as she was suffering from some mental problem and prior to committing suicide, she had made some attempts for committing suicide.

He submits even otherwise from the statement of father of deceased that initially there was no demand of dowry and deceased was in a very comfortable position in her in- laws house but after delivering the second child i.e. the girl and as such the in- laws created problem for her and started harassing her.
However, he submits that all those allegations are false and fabricated.
There was nothing like that and both the daughters have been accepted not only by the present applicant but also by his parents.
He submits that both the daughters are minor aged about 3 and 5 years and there is no one in teh family to look after them properly.
The father i.e the present applicant is also in jail since 01.06.2022.
He further submits that material witnesses have been examined, as such present applicant shall be released on bail.

On the other hand, counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that in view of the statements of witnesses and the circumstances as existing in this case, it is clear that the deceased had committed suicide as she was being harassed by the present applicant and other co-accused persons, and therefore, bail application deserves to be dismissed.

Considering the aforesaid and taking note of the fact that applicant has two minor daughters and there is no one in the family to look after them and to take care of them, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance on the dates given by it.

I t is further directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 437(3)
of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE Sateesh Prakash Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18485313/
